Validation rules, inferred schemas and synthetic stand-ins

Source: vignettes/validation-rules-and-synthetic-data.Rmd
validation-rules-and-synthetic-data.Rmd

A capsule says what shape its data must have. This vignette covers the three tools for stating and checking that shape: explicit rules, a schema inferred from a known-good table, and a synthetic stand-in generated from the schema when the portal is unreachable.

Rules

A rule is a name, a predicate and optionally a column. Row-wise rules report how many rows fail and which; table-wise rules take the whole data frame. A fatal severity stops the pipeline; a warning is recorded.

df <- data.frame(id = c(1, 2, 2), age = c(30, -5, 40),
                 start = c(1, 5, 3), end = c(2, 4, 9))

rules <- list(
  rule("age_non_negative", function(v) v >= 0, column = "age"),
  rule("id_unique", function(v) !anyDuplicated(v), column = "id", severity = "fatal"),
  rule("dates_ordered", function(d) all(d$start <= d$end))
)

issues <- validate_rules(df, rules)
names(issues)
#> [1] "age_non_negative" "id_unique"        "dates_ordered"
issues$age_non_negative$n_failed
#> [1] 1
issues$age_non_negative$rows
#> [1] 2

Clean data produces nothing:

clean <- data.frame(id = 1:3, age = c(30, 31, 40), start = 1:3, end = 4:6)
length(validate_rules(clean, rules))
#> [1] 0

Two behaviours matter for trust. A rule for an absent column is skipped, not failed: a missing column is the schema’s finding to report. And a rule that errors is a failure, never a silent pass:

length(validate_rules(data.frame(id = 1:3), rules[1:2]))
#> [1] 0
broken <- list(rule("bad", function(v) stop("boom"), column = "age"))
validate_rules(clean, broken)$bad$message
#> [1] "Rule 'bad' failed (rule could not be evaluated: boom)"

Ready-made rules

Common checks have constructors so the intent is in the name:

rules2 <- list(
  rule_not_null("id"),
  rule_unique("id", severity = "fatal"),
  rule_between("age", 0, 120),
  rule_in_set("grade", c("a", "b", "c")),
  rule_regex("code", "^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$"),
  rule_within_n_mads("score", n = 3),
  rule_col_count(6, severity = "fatal")
)
length(rules2)
#> [1] 7

rule_increasing(), rule_distinct_rows() and rule_complete_rows() complete the set. apply_schema_validation() runs a rule list and stops on any fatal issue, which is the call a pipeline makes.

Inferring a schema

Given a table known to be right, infer_schema() pins what can be pinned: column names and types, numeric ranges with a little slack, and the level set of categorical columns (up to max_levels, so free text is not mistaken for a code list):

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:100,
  score = stats::runif(100, 0, 10),
  grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 100, TRUE),
  note = paste0("free text ", 1:100),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
sch <- infer_schema(df)
sch$expected_value_sets
#> $grade
#> [1] "a" "b" "c"

It validates the table it was learned from, and catches a vanished column or a new category:

length(validate_schema(df, list(schema = sch)))
#> [1] 0
length(validate_schema(df[, -3], list(schema = sch))) > 0
#> [1] TRUE
bad <- df
bad$grade[1] <- "z"
length(validate_schema(bad, list(schema = sch))) > 0
#> [1] TRUE

A schema goes into the capsule’s provenance record; validate_schema() is what verify_capsule() runs on a fresh download.

Synthetic stand-ins

When the portal is down, the pipeline should still run end to end on data of the right shape, clearly marked as synthetic. A recipe names each column’s generator:

recipe <- list(
  n_rows = 20, seed = 42,
  columns = list(
    year   = list(type = "sample", values = list(2024, 2025)),
    alert  = list(type = "bernoulli", p = 0.2),
    visits = list(type = "poisson", lambda = 3, min = 1),
    id     = list(type = "id_pattern", pattern = "p-{seq:05d}")
  )
)
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
res <- make_synthetic_csv(recipe, out)
res$rows
#> [1] 20
res$seed
#> [1] 42

df <- utils::read.csv(out)
dim(df)
#> [1] 20  4
names(df)
#> [1] "year"   "alert"  "visits" "id"
head(df, 3)
#>   year alert visits      id
#> 1 2024    No      4 p-00001
#> 2 2024    No      7 p-00002
#> 3 2024   Yes      4 p-00003

The seed makes the stand-in reproducible; n_rows overrides the recipe’s own count. A <path>.synthetic sidecar file is written beside the CSV (the file itself stays a plain table), and the capsule checks read that marker, so a synthetic run can never be mistaken for a result:

make_synthetic_csv(recipe, tempfile(fileext = ".csv"), n_rows = 5)$rows
#> [1] 5

make_synthetic_column() generates one column from a spec, for building a table piece by piece or for testing a generator.

Putting them together

  1. On the first, trusted download: infer_schema(), then add the rules the schema cannot express (ordering between columns, cross-table consistency) and pin both.
  2. On every later run: validate_schema() and validate_rules(); stop on fatal.
  3. When the source is unreachable: make_synthetic_csv() from the pinned schema, run the pipeline, and let the synthetic marker say what the output is.
